insights.headline: MCX gold ends the week 4.1% lower at Rs 1.36 lakh as Fed hike bets keep bullion under pressure
insights.summary: Spot gold steadied near $3,890 after a 10th weekly fall in 12, its worst stretch since 1989, as US inflation kept December Fed hike bets alive and 10-year yields near 5.13%. MCX gold fell 4.1% on the week to Rs 1.36 lakh per 10 g and silver nearly 5% to Rs 1.76 lakh per kg, with COMEX gold down almost 5% to $3,886 an ounce. In India, lower prices drew firm festive and wedding-season buying, with premiums up to $8 an ounce, while Senco Gold's first-half revenue rose 52% and gemstone sales surged 40%. Silver slipped below $50, down 3.8% on the week on the London fix.
points: MCX gold fell 4.1% on the week to Rs 1.36 lakh per 10 g; silver slid nearly 5% to Rs 1.76 lakh per kg.
Spot gold held near $3,890 after a 10th weekly fall in 12, the worst run since 1989.
Silver slipped below $50, down 3.8% on the week, even as the market heads for a sixth straight annual supply deficit.
India's gold demand stayed firm on festive buying; premiums rose to $8 an ounce as prices fell.
Goldman Sachs cut its year-end gold call to $4,150 an ounce and its 2027 call to $4,800 an ounce.

brief.headline: Gold steadies near $3,890 after worst run since 1989
brief.summary: Spot gold held near $3,890, MCX gold near Rs 1.36 lakh per 10 g after a 10th weekly fall in 12; silver below $50.

bullets.text: MarketWatch says US jobs, CPI and PPI data since November 6 lifted the dollar and yields near 5.13%, keeping December Fed hike bets alive.
Lower prices drew festive and wedding-season buying as premiums doubled to $8 an ounce; the rupee outlook improved on returning inflows.
Watch the Fed's December 9 decision, due 00:30 IST on December 10, and US jobs data on December 4 for the next steer on rates.

trending.title: Fed hike bets keep bullion under pressure
trending.summary: Hotter US jobs, CPI and PPI data since November 6 lifted the dollar and yields, keeping December hike bets alive; gold fell about 4-5% on the week and silver slipped below $50.

trending.title: India buys the dip
trending.summary: Lower prices drew firm festive and wedding-season buying, premiums doubled to $8 an ounce, and jeweller Senco Gold's first-half revenue rose 52%.

trending.title: Silver's $50 test
trending.summary: Silver fell below $50 an ounce and closed the week near $49.12, down more than 5%, even as ETF selling masked a sixth straight annual supply deficit.

trending.title: Custody shifts east
trending.summary: Singapore opened a 500-tonne sovereign gold vault for foreign central banks, with tax relief from April 2027 and a clearing system due by March 2027.

items.title: Gold prices drop 4.1% to Rs 1.36 lakh, silver slides nearly 5% to Rs 1.76 lakh on MCX
items.summary: December gold futures fell Rs 5,847, or 4.1%, to Rs 1.36 lakh per 10 g this week, while silver slid Rs 8,791, nearly 5%, to Rs 1.76 lakh per kg. COMEX gold dropped almost 5% to $3,886 an ounce and silver 5.4% to $49.12, as a firm dollar and rising yields kept December Fed hike bets alive. Analysts expect volatility ahead, with inflation data, FOMC minutes and US jobs figures due.

items.title: Gold Makes Worst Losing Run in 4 Decades, Silver Plunge Tests $50 Again
items.summary: Gold fell for a 10th week in 12, its worst such stretch since 1989, fixing around $3,890 an ounce after a $150 weekly drop as strong US inflation data lifted bond yields; silver slipped below $50, down 3.8% on the week.

items.title: Rate-hike bets keep gold on track for worst week in four months
items.summary: Spot gold held near $3,880 an ounce on Friday, up 0.1% after briefly touching $3,923 on the US producer-price data, and stayed set for a weekly drop of about 4.5%, its worst week since early June. October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month, below the 0.4% forecast, and traders put December quarter-point hike odds at 91.4%. Silver fell 1.9% to $49.05 an ounce, also headed for a weekly loss.

items.title: Gold and silver are supposed to protect against inflation. So why are both metals tumbling instead?
items.summary: MarketWatch's Michael Kramer writes that jobs, CPI and PPI data since November 6 pushed rates and the dollar higher, giving the Fed reason to raise rates in December and signal more hikes in 2027. Gold has slipped from a peak near $5,500 early in the year toward $3,900-$4,000 support, and silver has dipped back below $50.

items.title: Gold, silver prices ahead of wedding season: Down over 4% this week - Investors guide before US Fed Dec meeting
items.summary: Gold and silver fell sharply ahead of India's wedding season, offering some relief to buyers, but the correction has raised questions over whether the sell-off has further to run. MCX gold ended Friday at Rs 1,36,750 per 10 g, down about 4.6% on the week, and silver at Rs 1,76,543 per kg, down nearly 5%, after hotter-than-expected US inflation strengthened bets on a December Fed rate hike.

items.title: Goldman Sachs cuts year-end gold price target to $4,150/oz, 2027 target to $4,800/oz
items.summary: Goldman Sachs has cut its year-end gold target to $4,150 an ounce from $4,650 and its end-2027 target to $4,800 from $5,400, citing the Federal Reserve's hawkish shift and another expected hike in December. The bank still sees central-bank buying averaging 60 tonnes a month supporting prices, with support returning once the Fed starts cutting rates in the second half of 2027.

items.title: India gold demand stays firm as lower prices draw festive buying
items.summary: India’s gold market stayed firm as lower prices drew festive and wedding-season buying, with domestic prices around Rs 137,000 per 10 g after touching Rs 135,530, their lowest since March 23; dealers quoted premiums up to $8 an ounce, double the previous week.

items.title: Gold & Silver Volatility Ahead: Inflation, Fed, West Asia
items.summary: Analysts expect a volatile week for gold and silver as traders weigh inflation readings from major economies, signals from the US Federal Reserve and developments in West Asia. Both metals fell sharply last week on domestic and international exchanges as a firmer dollar and higher bond yields kept December Fed hike bets alive.

items.title: Gold Price Slips to Key Support as Fed Rate Risks and GLD ETF Outflows Build
items.summary: Gold slipped to a key support level as risks of a December Federal Reserve rate hike and outflows from the SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) built, adding to the selling pressure on bullion after a week of sharp losses.

items.title: Silver's 6th Annual Deficit Masks a Surplus as ETF Selling Adds Supply
items.summary: Metals Focus and the Silver Institute now expect a sixth straight annual silver deficit of 35 million ounces in 2026, narrower than the 46.3 million ounces forecast in April. But silver funds are expected to release 45 million ounces over the year, flipping the balance to a 10 million ounce surplus. Coin and bar demand is forecast at 215 million ounces, down 2%.

items.title: Singapore Makes a $65 Billion Bet on the Future of Gold
items.summary: Singapore has launched a sovereign gold custody service with capacity for 500 tonnes of bullion, targeting foreign central banks and sovereign institutions, as investors shift metal to Asia amid geopolitical uncertainty. Tax relief on wholesale gold services takes effect in April 2027, and the Singapore Exchange's clearing system is due to start live trading by March 2027.

items.title: Senco Gold H1 revenue rises 52 pc to Rs 5,115 crore; adds 14 showrooms
items.summary: Senco Gold's consolidated revenue rose 52% year on year to Rs 5,114.8 crore in the first half of FY27, with retail revenue up 40% and same-store sales up 30%, as festive demand stayed firm despite high prices. The jeweller added 14 showrooms to reach 215 across India and plans 10-12 more in the second half. Profit after tax rose 22% to Rs 187.8 crore in the half year.

items.title: Indians look beyond gold and diamonds as coloured gemstone sales surge 40%
items.summary: Coloured gemstone sales rose 40% during the festive season as affluent Indian buyers looked beyond gold and diamond jewellery for exclusivity and distinctive designs, jewellers say. Rare Paraiba tourmalines cost about Rs 5 lakh per carat, and bespoke jewellery starts at about Rs 7 lakh, with studded jewellery taking a growing share of organised retailers' sales.

items.title: Govt notifies commodity contracts as financial products at GIFT IFSC
items.summary: The government has notified commodity trading contracts as financial products under the IFSCA Act, bringing commodity trading by IFSC units within the financial-products framework at GIFT City and paving the way for global trading firms to operate from there.

items.title: Rupee outlook improves as foreign inflows return despite wider October trade deficit: Axis Bank
items.summary: The rupee's outlook has improved as foreign inflows returned despite October's trade deficit widening to $40 billion, Axis Bank Research says. Foreign investors bought nearly $6 billion of Indian equities in early November, and the bank sees the current account deficit contained near 1% of GDP, with the rupee at 94.24 to the dollar after touching 93.69 on November 11.

items.title: India gold ETF, equity fund inflows ease in Oct
items.summary: Investments in Indian gold ETFs fell 22% in October to Rs 3,474 crore ($370.57 million), AMFI data showed, after fund houses suspended fresh subscriptions and bulk purchases ahead of the festive season. Equity fund inflows also eased about 14% to Rs 32,994 crore, as the curbs aim to limit gold imports while the rupee hovers near record lows.

items.title: India's current account deficit seen widening to USD 57 billion in FY27 on higher imports: ICICI Bank
items.summary: ICICI Bank expects India's current account deficit to widen to $57 billion, or 1.4% of GDP, in FY27, with the goods trade deficit at $380 billion. October's merchandise deficit hit a 12-month high near $40 billion even as exports rose 45% to a record $49 billion, and the bank expects gold imports to stay moderate.
